sections.body: The AI Physician covers ten areas where artificial intelligence is doing concrete work in medicine today. In diagnostic imaging, models read scans for patterns that radiologists may miss. In clinical documentation, ambient systems listen to patient visits and draft notes. In drug discovery, simulations screen molecules before any lab work. In intensive care, predictive models flag patients whose vital signs may soon worsen. These are working systems in hospitals and labs, not future promises.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field is uneven. Imaging and documentation tools are widely deployed and have clear benchmarks, but they still make errors and require human review. Genomics and drug discovery show strong results in research, yet translating those results into approved treatments is slow and expensive. Predictive analytics in intensive care can alert staff, but false alarms and inconsistent data limit trust. The site tracks 1000 medical AI models, which shows the scale of activity, but also the fragmentation. Honest limits include bias in training data, poor performance outside the hospitals where models were built, and unresolved questions about liability when a model contributes to harm.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for how AI reads scans would start with Diagnostic Imaging and Radiology, while Genomic Medicine and Precision Therapeutics covers tailoring treatment to a person's genes. Clinical Documentation and Ambient Intelligence explains the tools that listen and write, and Surgical Robotics and Navigation covers machines in the operating room. Predictive Patient Analytics and Intensive Care is the place for early warning systems, and Drug Discovery and Molecular Simulation follows the path from molecule to medicine. Telemedicine and Triage covers remote assessment, Epidemiology and Population Health looks at whole communities, and Neuroinformatics and the Brain connects AI to neuroscience. Governance, Compliance and Medical Device Security closes the section with the rules and risks around these devices.
